title: The Letter with Two Possible Readers
title_ja: 二人の読み手を持つ手紙
fact_notes: 人物・町・行事・数値や結果は架空の事例。実在の統計や研究結果ではない。参考リンクは制作台帳であり、実証資料ではない。

sentences.en: In a creative writing class, the students received an imaginary letter written by a traveler who was about to leave a coastal town.
sentences.ja: 創作の授業で、生徒は海辺の町を去ろうとする旅行者が書いた架空の手紙を受け取った。

sentences.en: The letter described a familiar harbor, a quiet morning, and a promise to return when the weather became warmer.
sentences.ja: 手紙にはなじみのある港、静かな朝、暖かくなれば戻るという約束が描かれていた。

sentences.en: Although the message sounded personal, the writer had deliberately removed the name of the person who would receive it.
sentences.ja: 個人的な手紙のように思えたが、作者は受取人の名前を意図的に削除していた。

sentences.en: The students were asked to propose two different readers for whom the words could have a reasonable meaning.
sentences.ja: 生徒は、その言葉が筋の通った意味を持つような異なる読み手を二人提案するよう求められた。

sentences.en: One group imagined that the letter was addressed to a close friend who still lived near the harbor.
sentences.ja: 一つのグループは手紙が今も港の近くに住む親友に宛てられたと想像した。

sentences.en: They interpreted the promise as evidence that the traveler wished to maintain an important personal relationship despite the distance.
sentences.ja: 彼らは約束を、距離があっても大切な人間関係を維持したいという証拠として解釈した。

sentences.en: Another group suggested that the writer was speaking to a younger version of himself through an imaginary message.
sentences.ja: 別のグループは、作者が架空のメッセージを通じて若い頃の自分に語りかけていると提案した。

sentences.en: In their reading, the harbor represented memories that the traveler feared losing as his life continued to change.
sentences.ja: その読み方では、港は生活が変化する中で失うことを恐れた記憶を表していた。

sentences.en: The teacher encouraged both groups to identify details that supported their interpretations and details that might cause difficulties.
sentences.ja: 教師は両グループにそれぞれの解釈を支える細部と問題になり得る細部を指摘するよう促した。

sentences.en: For example, a reference to a shared breakfast appeared to support the idea that another person had been present.
sentences.ja: 例えば、一緒に朝食を取ったという記述は別の人物がいたという考えを支持しているように見えた。

sentences.en: However, a description of an old photograph could be understood as either a shared memory or a private reflection.
sentences.ja: しかし古い写真の記述は、共有された思い出とも個人的な回想とも理解できた。

sentences.en: Rather than declare both readings equally convincing, the groups considered the strength and limitations of the available textual evidence.
sentences.ja: 二つの読み方が同じように説得力があると宣言せず、本文の証拠の強さと限界を考えた。

sentences.en: The students then rewrote the opening of the letter so that each intended reader would become easier to identify.
sentences.ja: 次に生徒は意図した読み手が特定しやすくなるよう手紙の冒頭を書き直した。

sentences.en: One group added a direct greeting, while the other introduced a sentence reflecting on the passing of time.
sentences.ja: 一方は直接の呼びかけを加え、もう一方は時間の経過を振り返る文を導入した。

sentences.en: They discovered that even a small addition could guide readers toward a particular understanding of the entire message.
sentences.ja: 小さな追加でさえ、メッセージ全体の特定の理解へ読み手を導くことができると分かった。

sentences.en: The activity also helped them appreciate why an author might deliberately leave certain relationships unstated in a literary work.
sentences.ja: 活動を通じて、作者が文学作品で特定の関係を意図的に明示しない理由も理解できた。

sentences.en: The class concluded that uncertainty about a text does not necessarily prevent readers from developing meaningful interpretations of it.
sentences.ja: クラスは文章の不確実さが必ずしも意味のある解釈を形成する妨げにはならないと結論づけた。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, an imaginative interpretation must still be examined in relation to the actual language used by the writer.
sentences.ja: それでも想像力に富む解釈は作者が実際に使った言葉と関連づけて検討されなければならない。

sentences.en: Readers should be prepared to reconsider their ideas when another interpretation explains the details more successfully.
sentences.ja: 別の解釈が細部をよりうまく説明するとき、読み手は自分の考えを再検討する準備をすべきだ。

sentences.en: The letter demonstrated how reading literature involves both the freedom to imagine and the responsibility to examine evidence carefully.
sentences.ja: 手紙は文学の読解には想像の自由と証拠を慎重に検討する責任の両方があることを示した。

questions.prompt: What information had been removed from the letter?
questions.explanation_ja: 受取人名が削除されていた。

questions.prompt: What were students asked to propose?
options: Two possible readers of the letter.
questions.explanation_ja: 異なる二人の読み手を考えた。

questions.prompt: Who was the intended reader according to the first group?
options: A school teacher who lived abroad.
A close friend living near the harbor.
A person who had never met the traveler.
The traveler at an older age.

questions.prompt: What did the harbor symbolize in the second group's reading?
options: A business opportunity for the traveler.
A place the traveler had never visited.
An obstacle that prevented all travel.
questions.explanation_ja: 失われるのを恐れた記憶。

questions.prompt: Which detail appeared to support the presence of another person?
questions.explanation_ja: 一緒に朝食を取った記述。

questions.prompt: Why did the groups examine limitations of their readings?
options: They had decided that evidence was irrelevant.
They needed to choose a real harbor to visit.
They wanted to assess whether the text supported their ideas.
They wanted to remove every uncertain detail.
questions.explanation_ja: 解釈を支える根拠とその限界を検討した。

options: The description of a new town.
questions.explanation_ja: 手紙の冒頭を書き直した。

questions.prompt: What did adding a small detail demonstrate?
options: All literary texts have only one possible reader.
Wording can influence how readers interpret a whole message.
A greeting always destroys the meaning of a letter.
The ending of a text is never important.
questions.explanation_ja: 小さな追加が全体の理解を導くことがある。
再検討するという意味。

options: Literary interpretation requires imagination together with attention to textual evidence.
A literary reader should accept every interpretation as equally strong.
A missing name makes a text impossible to understand.
Authors should never leave a relationship unstated.
questions.explanation_ja: 想像と本文の根拠の両方が必要。

grammar.explanation_ja: despiteは〜にもかかわらずという前置詞。

grammar.focus: could be understood as either a shared memory or a private reflection
grammar.explanation_ja: either A or Bは二つの可能性を示す。

grammar.focus: when another interpretation explains the details more successfully
grammar.explanation_ja: when節は再検討すべき条件を示す。

discourse.role_ja: 個人的な手紙と受取人名の不在を対比。
一つに解釈を決められない例を示す。
解釈の自由と証拠の必要性を対比。

paraphrases.source: Although the message sounded personal, the writer had deliberately removed the name of the person who would receive it.
paraphrases.rewrite: The message seemed private, yet its writer had intentionally left out the recipient's name.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 個人的な文章だが受取人名がなかった。

paraphrases.source: They interpreted the promise as evidence that the traveler wished to maintain an important personal relationship despite the distance.
paraphrases.rewrite: They believed the promise showed a wish to preserve a valued relationship even though the people were far apart.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 距離があっても関係を保ちたいと解釈。

paraphrases.source: However, a description of an old photograph could be understood as either a shared memory or a private reflection.
paraphrases.rewrite: The old photograph might suggest a memory held by two people or a person's thoughts about the past.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 古い写真には二つの解釈がある。

paraphrases.source: Readers should be prepared to reconsider their ideas when another interpretation explains the details more successfully.
paraphrases.rewrite: Readers should be willing to rethink their reading if a different one accounts for the textual details better.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: より説明力のある読み方なら再検討する。

cloze.explanation_ja: 作者は名前を削除した。
根拠の限界を考慮した。
別の解釈がより適切なら再考。
